title: Advocate for Equity and Inclusion at Palm Beach County School Board!
description:
In April the Palm Beach County Public School Board held an emergency meeting to remove the policies that enabled people of all identities and backgrounds to feel welcome and do their best work. At the same time,  we know that this board and community still believes in these values. 

We understand the pressure that the board was under but we must mobilize to encourage them to revisit their decision. Their policies have always followed the law and the courts are already delaying Title VI policy enforcement.

Every child deserves to feel seen, heard, and supported in the classroom.  The best way to serve a diverse student population is to have diverse, talented educators and professionals serving them. When students feel like they belong, they’re more likely to thrive—academically and personally.

Please join us in advocating for Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Fairness at Palm Beach School Board Meeting Wednesday June 4th at 5:00! 

Your stories and your voice will go far in helping make the change our students and community deserves!

title: Webinar with Reverend Dr. Allan Boesak

description:
Hui Aloha ‘O Hawaii would like to invite you to a webinar with the Reverend Dr. Allan Boesak 

Saturday June 7, at 8:00 am

Dr. Boesak, author and global human rights activist, is a South African theologian who played a leading role in the anti-apartheid struggle. Dr. Boesak has received numerous awards and accolades for his work. These include the Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Award, the Martin Luther King Jr. Peace Award, and the King Hintsa Bravery Award from the Royal Xhosa House. He also holds twelve honorary degrees from prestigious institutions such as Yale University and the University of Geneva. Dr. Boesak will be sharing his wisdom on ways we can maintain hope in politically difficult times and challenging us on ways we can respond within our communities and our nation. 

This talk is cosponsored by Hui Aloha ‘O Hawaii Indivisible, Kaua’i’s Justice and Witness Committee, and the HCUCC Justice & Witness Missional Team. This webinar will take place on Zoom and will include a Q & session. Please join us!  All are welcome!

description:
Please join us for this highly rated Resistance Lab 101 training, developed by Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal. 

The Resistance Lab training was developed specifically for this moment, utilizing the tools and frameworks from numerous organizations specializing in nonviolent resistance movements around the country and around the world as well as Congresswoman Jayapal’s organizing background for 20 years prior to Congress. The training explores how democracies fall, how movements around the world have responded, and the tools and tactics available to us to resist. 

The training goals are to help educate people on how to turn anger, fear and frustration into effective, non-violent action. We want to channel people towards current organizing opportunities while also helping to ensure we are strike-ready and street-ready for any large coordinated actions or opportunities that may come as a result of the destruction of our democracy. 

Congresswoman Jayapal recommends this training is be done in-person in our community. Prior attendees loved being in community with others for this training and the breakout sessions are extremely highly valued in their evaluations. This is a great way to channel energy into immediate action, but also to train on the most effective forms of action and provide frameworks to understand how Democratic backsliding happens around the world and what we can do about it.

title: NO KINGS Mankato
description:
Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.

Join us in Mankato Saturday, June 14, from 11-12:30 pm to say:

We are united against kings.

No using OUR tax dollars to pay for HIS party.

They’ve gone too far: This is bigger than political disagreement. They’ve defied our courts, deported American citizens, disappeared people off the streets, and slashed our services—all while orchestrating a massive giveaway to their billionaire allies. Enough is enough. For anyone who thinks he’s gone too far, this movement is for you.

LOGISTICS

We will rally on the sidewalks along two busy side streets in Mankato, Warren St and South Broad St: north on Broad from Warren to Cherry, and 1-2 blocks east and west of Broad on Warren.

Bring a sign or two, water, cash for emergencies, and weather-appropriate clothing. The nearest bathrooms are a couple of blocks away, so be prepared for that too.

A core principle behind all NO KINGS events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. We ask participants to obey traffic and other laws and be mindful of pedestrians using the sidewalks. There will be a police presence at the event but we will rely on our own peacekeepers, volunteers, and you to assist with de-escalation. If asked by leaders or police to disperse, please do so at once.

This event is co-sponsored by Indivisible St. Peter/Greater Mankato and ACLU MN and COPAL MN. Thank you so much for standing with us!

title: Debrief & Strategy Call
description:
Join Vote Forward Executive Director Yasmin Radjy and Senior Director of Data & Research Emily Wasserman as we debrief the results of our 2024 letter writing campaigns and share strategies for what comes next.

Since the 2024 election, Vote Forward has engaged in rigorous analysis and deep reflection to inform our response to this challenging moment. We’re now ready to debut the results transparently and introduce our next steps. 

Every cycle, Vote Forward runs numerous RCT (randomized controlled trials) to test the effectiveness of our voter turnout programs. Then, in our continued pursuit of innovation and commitment to transparency, we share our learnings with our volunteers and supporters, peer organizations, and the public. 

We know there’s too much at stake to keep doing the same old thing—and figuring out what works in our new political, media, and cultural landscape requires intense evidence-driven experimentation and testing. This is the time for creativity, innovation, and big bets to win the elections that will matter most to the future of democracy.

By embracing what the Vote Forward community does best—developing and testing smart voter contact strategies powered by volunteers and sharing our learnings—we can be part of the solution. RSVP for the call Monday, June 9th at 8pm ET/ 5pm PT.

title: NCDC Supports Juneteenth at Meyer Amphitheater
description:
Join the clubs and caucuses of the PBC Democratic Executive Committee as we celebrate Juneteenth on 6/22/25 from 5-10.  Volunteer to help recruit leaders, register voters, and talk about Democratic Values. 

Juneteenth commemorates the emancipation of enslaved African Americans in Texas on June 19, 1865, marking the end of slavery in the United States. 
It's a time for reflection, remembrance, and celebrating the progress towards freedom and equality, as well as recognizing that the fight for justice and equity continues. 

Juneteenth, also known as "Freedom Day" or "Emancipation Day," commemorates the arrival of Union soldiers in Galveston, Texas, announcing that enslaved people were free, two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was issued. 

Juneteenth celebrations often include prayer services, speeches, educational events, and community gatherings with food, music, and dancing. 

While Juneteenth originated in Texas, it's now celebrated across the United States and even internationally as a reminder of the ongoing struggle for freedom and equality. 

Juneteenth is a time to acknowledge the progress made while also recognizing that the fight for true equality continues, including issues like voter suppression and racial justice. 

Many see Juneteenth as a connection to other emancipation celebrations across the African diaspora, highlighting a shared history of striving for freedom and independence.

Multnomah County Democrats

The rise of authoritarianism is real, and we are fighting back --- as People of Faith, as Hooisers, and as Union Members --- United as Americans!
